column9:
As my role has evolved to include significant technical work (data automation, Python, analytics infrastructure) and I've expressed interest in transitioning toward product management, these are areas where Joe's strengths—soft skills, people management, and AEC industry expertise—don't fully overlap.

Joe has been supportive by encouraging me to lean on existing relationships, like my PM Katarina, for PM mentorship. To build on this, Joe could explore ways to be more actively involved in shaping development paths for team members whose growth areas fall outside his direct expertise—whether that's facilitating introductions to mentors in other parts of Autodesk or staying more connected to the technical aspects of the work to provide more specific feedback. This would complement his already-strong interpersonal support with more targeted career development guidance.

Joe consistently demonstrates several One ORBIT behaviors:

TRUSTED: Joe creates an environment where I feel safe being honest about my career aspirations—even when that includes exploring other roles. His consistent support builds genuine trust. He follows through on commitments (like securing immigration sponsorship) and shows empathy for the whole person, not just the employee.

OPTIMISTIC: Joe brings an encouraging and positive presence to our interactions. Even when discussing challenges, he maintains a supportive tone that makes difficult conversations easier to have.

Joe has made a meaningful impact as a people manager this year, particularly in supporting his direct reports' growth and wellbeing. Two examples stand out:

Career Development Support: When I expressed interest in exploring other roles within Autodesk, Joe responded with genuine encouragement rather than defensiveness. He supported my exploration openly, demonstrating that he prioritizes his team members' long-term career growth over short-term retention concerns.

Advocacy for Immigration Sponsorship: When I needed Autodesk to sponsor my Canadian permanent residency application, Joe advocated strongly on my behalf. He navigated the organizational process to secure budget approval for legal support, ensuring I had the resources needed for this important life milestone. This required cross-functional coordination and persistence, and his advocacy made a tangible difference in my ability to build a stable future.

column9:
Defining squad boundaries
I believe there are still opportunities for improvement in terms of clarifying the Engagement squad’s remit and areas of ownership. Currently, there are overlaps - for example, with the First Strike squad and Content Strategy - that create friction and/or some communication overhead. In addition to experimentation, the squad could make a stronger impact by taking ownership of certain “always-on” initiatives around user engagement, such as onboarding emails and experiences to reduce churn. From a content strategy standpoint, I expect a very close collaboration through and after the migration of our Help center.

Vision for engagement in 6-18 months
Both as the Engagement squad lead and the manager of Adoption Specialists, Joe could make more impact by taking a more proactive stance on where our engagement and support strategy should be when Forma Industry Cloud becomes a reality. I see him as an important stakeholder in discussions about our support strategy (likely the main driver), future tooling, learning vision, and related areas. I also believe that this longer term vision will help define and evolve different team roles.
